cohort: Pregnant women giving birth at extremely preterm (23 0/7-27 6/7 weeks) and very preterm gestational ages (28 0/7-31 6/7 weeks) at Royal Brisbane and Womens Hospital, Queensland, Australia between 2016 and 2020
finding: Short-term maternal and neonatal outcomes did not significantly differ between classical caesarean sections and low transverse caesarean sections for extremely preterm or very preterm births.
mod_finding: While classical caesarean sections were associated with lower Apgar scores at 1 minute post-birth than low transverse caesarean sections at very preterm gestational ages, there was no statistical difference in the rates of intraoperative neonatal injuries or composite outcomes when corrected for low birth weight.
